Repair the provided Synecdoche discovery-to-deployment project.
Work in `/workspace/submission`; `run.py` is the JSON stdin/stdout entry point.
Extend its real offline discovery, calibration, backup and matching components.
Produce exact fragment, cluster, score, backup-tree and table certificates.
Replay atomic installs and interleaved flow epochs across model releases.
Account for range/exact banks retained by open flows, including classified ones.
Preserve the specified direction, priority, fallback and release-lifetime rules.
Read `/workspace/PROTOCOL.md` for complete schemas, arithmetic and boundaries.
`PROJECT.md` describes the supplied modules and offline CPU environment.
The pinned CPU packages and all installation files are already supplied locally.
No neural training, packet capture, network access or switch hardware is needed.
Return one complete JSON response; invalid requests return the specified error.
Submit the whole project with `run.py`, within the documented file/byte bounds.
Other regular project files are allowed; documented development caches are ignored.
Run `python3 check.py submission` from `/workspace` as a nonroot user.
The command prepares local wheels automatically and runs small public sanity cases.
All requirements apply beyond those cases; the public checker gives no score.
Your implementation must handle the whole published request budget in one process.


Work in /workspace. When finished run exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT
items.finalText:
The repair is complete. Here's a summary of the work:

## What was broken and how it was fixed

**`formats.py`** — request envelope: now rejects non-integer numeric tokens (`3.0`, `3e0`), duplicate keys, nonfinite constants, extra keys, trailing data, invalid UTF-8, depth > 32, and enforces every published row/value/operation bound plus the padding-suffix rule; a pre-pass validates flow lifecycle and per-epoch timestamp monotonicity.

**`offline_discovery/rule_generate.py`** — replaced the float/DBSCAN batch code with exact arithmetic: activation threshold decided by integer comparison (`offset>0 and offset²>spread`), maximal high runs, runs longer than `width` contributing the greatest-sum width window *including the final legal window* (earliest start on ties), pattern distance compared exactly as `S·9ᴬ·q² ≤ L·25ᴬ·p²`, per class/length clustering with the class-wide density minimum `max(2,ceil(m·ratio))`, core components, non-core attachment to the smallest-core-ID component, noise, and generalized intervals with trunc-toward-zero `isqrt` bounds.

**`offline_discovery/rule_remove.py`** — calibration: window matching against real prefixes, per-class hits, exact score `Cin/(Cout+1/10000)`, strict keep threshold (no forced backups), and exact-table accounting (distinct keys per length, 1514 excluded at every coordinate, clipped to `capacity.exact+1`).

**`online_matching/train_rf.py` / `match_p4.py`** — the pinned scikit-learn 1.4.2 backup tree with native node-order certificate (`[class]` leaves, `[feature,2·threshold,left,right]` branches) and the `2·feature ≤ 2·threshold` prediction path; per-release value→cluster bitmask tables giving the highest-priority suffix match.

**`sessions.py`** — the missing replay: atomic installs (`ok`/`busy`/`oversize`, unchanged state on failure), eviction of an unpinned current bank, separate range/exact pool accounting, banks pinned by open epochs (including classified ones) and evicted when the last flow closes, per-flow epoch counters, direction fixing from the first packet, and the idle → segment → limit → close decision rules.

## Verification
Public fixtures match exactly; independent brute-force references cross-check fragments, clustering, intervals, calibration, exact tables, the tree and 750 random replay traces; hand-written scenarios cover idle/limit/close commits, busy/oversize installs, pinned-bank retention and epoch counters; malformed-request cases all return `{"error":"invalid_request"}`. A request at the published budget (4096 fragments, 1M values, 218k operations) completes in ~6 s CPU with 228 MB RSS and no stderr output. (The local `check.py` cannot spawn its child here because the outer sandbox denies `setsid`; an equivalent harness with identical env reproduces the runner's child exactly.)
